answer: An agent economy can forge each identity through a sequential verifiable delay function: minting one identity requires a computation that cannot be sped up by running many machines in parallel, so it always takes a fixed wall-clock time, say one hour. A legitimate newcomer, a sparrow among larger agents, pays that hour once, but a Sybil attacker wanting ten thousand fake identities must pay ten thousand sequential hours. The ferrous rule is unforgiving: extra hardware buys no shortcut, so fake numbers stop being cheap.
